A named policy holds the first-factor mechanisms allowed (password, password-mfa, webauthn, spnego, wallet, federation; none allows every one) and the second factors allowed (password, securityKey, totp, recoveryCode, emailCode, emailLink, wallet; none leaves the realm's as it is). `default` allows every mechanism the realm's authentication policy allows.

ENFORCED at every browser sign-in to the application, in both modes: a person whose session stands on a mechanism the policy does not allow is sent to sign in again with one it does. One first-factor mechanism listed is also where the sign-in goes (`spnego` to /authn/spnego, `wallet` to /authn/wallet, `federation` to appFederationRelationship). The second factors only NARROW the realm's policy: one it has switched off stays off here.

A name no policy of this realm holds — written past the console — allows NO mechanism until the policy exists (STS-AUTHN-0536).

It is WRITTEN BY NOBODY: no protocol presents it, so it is editable and starts empty.

attributes.name: appPasskeyPolicy
attributes.from: the console, the management API, or by hand
attributes.what:
THE PASSKEY POLICY A SIGN-IN TO THIS APPLICATION IS HELD TO: `default` (or empty), or the name of a named passkey policy of this realm (Directory > Policies). It competes on precedence with the passkey policy each of the person's groups names (stsPasskeyPolicy): the lowest precedence applies, ties by name, and `default` where nothing names one.

A name no policy of this realm holds — written past the console — names nothing and is logged (STS-AUTHN-0537). A named passkey policy this attribute names cannot be deleted (STS-AUTHN-0538).

It is WRITTEN BY NOBODY: no protocol presents it, so it is editable and starts empty.

attributes.name: appLocalePolicy
attributes.from: the console, the management API, or by hand
attributes.what:
THE LOCALE POLICY A PAGE OR A MAIL FOR THIS APPLICATION FALLS BACK TO: `default` (or empty), or the name of a named locale policy of this realm (Directory > Policies). It decides the language a page is drawn in when the request, the person and the browser name none a catalog answers, and the preferredLanguage a person this application causes to be created is given. Where the person is known it competes on precedence with the locale policy each of the person's groups names (stsLocalePolicy): the lowest precedence applies, ties by name, and `default` where nothing names one.

A name no policy of this realm holds — written past the console — names nothing and is logged (STS-I18N-0013): `default` applies, as a language is all it decides. A named locale policy this attribute names cannot be deleted (STS-I18N-0014).

It is WRITTEN BY NOBODY: no protocol presents it, so it is editable and starts empty.

attributes.name: appPasswordPolicy
attributes.from: the console, the management API, or by hand
attributes.what:
THE PASSWORD POLICY A PASSWORD SET WHILE SIGNING IN TO THIS APPLICATION IS HELD TO: `default` (or empty), or the name of a named password policy of this realm (Directory > Policies). It competes on precedence with the password policy each of the person's groups names (stsPasswordPolicy): the lowest precedence applies, ties by name, and `default` where nothing names one. A door with no application in hand (the portal, the console, LDAP) ranks the groups' alone.

A name no policy of this realm holds — written past the console — names nothing, the group references still rank, and it is logged (STS-AUTHN-0539). A named password policy this attribute names cannot be deleted (STS-AUTHN-0540).

It is WRITTEN BY NOBODY: no protocol presents it, so it is editable and starts empty.

attributes.name: appPostLoginPolicy
attributes.from: the console, the management API, or by hand
attributes.what:
THE POST-LOGIN ACTIVITY POLICY A SIGN-IN TO THIS APPLICATION FOLLOWS: `default` (or empty), or the name of a named post-login policy of this realm (Directory > Policies). It competes on precedence with the post-login policy each of the person's groups names (stsPostLoginPolicy): the lowest precedence applies, ties by name, and `default` where nothing names one. A named policy with its activity off EXCLUDES a sign-in to this application where it wins.

It is read at the sign-in only: a started activity's reminder mail and the progress report know no application, and select by the person's groups alone.

A name no policy of this realm holds — written past the console — names nothing and is logged (STS-AUTHN-0542). A named post-login policy this attribute names cannot be deleted (STS-AUTHN-0543).

It is WRITTEN BY NOBODY: no protocol presents it, so it is editable and starts empty.

attributes.name: appFgaPolicy
attributes.from: this registry, when the application is created
attributes.what: The entry name in ou=policies of the fine-grained authorization policy this application owns, which decides each authorization detail of the types it declares once appFgaEnforced is TRUE.

attributes.name: appFgaEnforced
attributes.from: this registry, when fine-grained authorization is switched
attributes.what: TRUE when this application's fine-grained policy is enforced. Absent or FALSE means it is not, which is the default.

attributes.name: umaOwnsResources
attributes.from: the console, the management API, or by hand
attributes.what: TRUE when this UMA 2.0 resource server may register resources it OWNS ITSELF, through a protection API token obtained with client_credentials. Absent or FALSE, the default, means a PAT must be a person's (the code flow) and that person owns what it registers.

attributeSource.note: The source is one JSON value, stsAttributeSourceData.

objectClasses.name: top
objectClasses.what: The abstract class every entry carries.

objectClasses.name: stsAttributeSource
objectClasses.what: This service's class for one attribute source.

attributes.name: cn
attributes.what: The source id, the RDN.

attributes.name: stsAttributeSourceData
attributes.what: The whole definition as one JSON value. No password.

attributes.name: stsAttributeSourced
attributes.what: On a person: <source>:<attribute> a source wrote.

attributes.name: stsAttributeSourceSeen
attributes.what: On a person: <source>=<time> of the last read.

claimProvider.note: The record is one JSON value, stsClaimProviderData.

objectClasses.name: top
objectClasses.what: The abstract class every entry carries.

objectClasses.name: stsClaimProvider
objectClasses.what: This service's class for this register.

attributes.name: stsClaimProviderData
attributes.what: The claims provider's whole record as one JSON value: its issuer, endpoints, client identifier, authentication method, scope, the claims it answers and how they are delivered. Written by the console and the management API.

attributes.name: stsClaimProviderSecret
attributes.what: The client secret this service presents to the claims provider, sealed where a key-encryption key is configured. Withheld from every directory read.

objectClasses.name: device
objectClasses.what: cn, and the standard owner and description.

objectClasses.name: stsDevice
objectClasses.what: Every stsDevice* attribute below: the owner's kind, the applications, the keys, attestation, compliance, status, the descriptive labels, the enrolment and Native SSO.

attributes.name: cn
attributes.what: The device id, a UUID.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.what: The DN of its one owner: a person or an application.

attributes.name: stsDeviceOwnerKind
attributes.what: person or application.

attributes.name: description
attributes.what: Its label.

attributes.name: stsDeviceApplication
attributes.what: The DN of every application that used it.

attributes.name: stsDeviceKey
attributes.what: One JSON value per key: id, kind (x509, jwk, webauthn), thumbprint, label, added, addedBy, proof, attestation and the public material. Never a secret.

attributes.name: stsDeviceKeyThumbprint
attributes.what: <kind>:<thumbprint> per key, derived from stsDeviceKey on every write so an LDAP filter can find a device by its key.

attributes.name: stsDeviceCredentialId
attributes.what: The credential id of each linked WebAuthn key, derived from stsDeviceKey on every write so a sign-in finds its device by index.

attributes.name: stsDeviceAndroidKey
attributes.what: The id of each key attested by an Android chain whose serials were kept, derived from stsDeviceKey on every write so the Android attestation recheck reads only the devices holding one (#615).

attributes.name: stsDeviceAttestation
attributes.what: attested when any key's attestation was verified, else self-asserted. Derived on every write.

attributes.name: stsDeviceCompliance
attributes.what: compliant or not-compliant; absent is unknown.

attributes.name: stsDeviceComplianceChange

attributes.name: stsDeviceStatus

attributes.name: stsDeviceStatusChange

attributes.name: stsDeviceRiskLevel
attributes.what: LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH (CAEP's risk levels); absent is unassessed. Set by risk scoring and by a compromise.

attributes.name: stsDeviceRiskChange
attributes.what: JSON: the last risk level change — level, previous, at, source (risk, compromise, admin), actor, reason.

attributes.name: stsDeviceBrowser
attributes.what: JSON: a remembered browser's state (#265) — the token generation, when it and the one before were issued, the browser it was bound to, and when the second factor was last given on it. No token and no secret.

attributes.name: stsDevicePlatform
attributes.what: ios, ipados, android, macos, windows, linux, chromeos or other.

attributes.name: stsDeviceModel
attributes.what: Descriptive.

attributes.name: stsDeviceOs
attributes.what: Descriptive.

attributes.name: stsDeviceEnrolment
attributes.what: JSON: method (native-sso, admin, portal, est, scep), at, actor.

attributes.name: stsDeviceSecretHash

attributes.name: stsDeviceSession
attributes.what: The sign-on session the secret is good for.

attributes.name: stsDeviceLastUsed
attributes.what: When it was last used, ISO 8601.

objectClasses.name: top
objectClasses.what: The abstract class every entry carries.

objectClasses.name: applicationProcess
objectClasses.what: The same registered class ou=applications uses, and for the same reason: it is the one that fits a party in a protocol at all, and it brings cn, description, seeAlso, ou and l with it.

objectClasses.name: stsFederation
objectClasses.what: INVENTED. No registered LDAP schema has a federation partner, because every product that stores one (AD FS, Shibboleth, Keycloak, Ping) keeps it in its own database. These are this service's own names in the way stsApplication's already are.

attributes.name: fedId
attributes.what: THE KEY: a short name an operator chose, unique across both roles. It is the RDN as well, unlike an application's, because this register is CONFIGURED rather than observed — nobody has to accept whatever a protocol presented, so the id can simply be required to be RDN-safe and short.

attributes.name: cn
attributes.what: The RDN value, equal to fedId. Unlike an application entry there is no digest case here: an id that would not fit is refused at creation rather than hashed.

attributes.name: fedName
attributes.what: What to call the partner on a page. The id is the name when none is given, because inventing a friendly name would be inventing a fact.

attributes.name: fedRole
attributes.what: WHICH END THIS SERVICE IS: service-provider (it consumes) or identity-provider (it asserts). One relationship is one direction — see the header.

attributes.name: fedProtocol
attributes.what: One of saml2, saml11, wsfed, oidc, oauth2 — the five sign-in protocols — or ssf, a partner that only sends Shared Signals and signs nobody in.

attributes.name: fedProvider
attributes.what: THE CONSUMER OR SOCIAL PROVIDER THIS RELATIONSHIP IS (google, discord, github, generic-oidc, generic-oauth2), or empty for an enterprise partner. Set when the relationship is created and never changed: the provider's profile wrote its endpoints onto this entry then, and supplies at every sign-in where the subject, the address and its verification come from. A relationship naming a provider is in the consumer category, which a realm turns on with federation.consumerProviders.

attributes.name: fedPeer
attributes.what: THE PARTNER'S OWN IDENTIFIER, in whatever its protocol calls it: a SAML entityID, an OpenID Connect issuer, a WS-Federation wtrealm. On a service-provider-side relationship it is CHECKED — an assertion whose Issuer is not this string is refused — which is why it is not merely documentation, and since 2026-09-12 it is REQUIRED there: a relationship without it is not fully configured.

attributes.name: fedLocalEntityId
attributes.what: WHAT THIS SERVICE IS CALLED TO THIS PARTNER, when that is not the name this service derives. Empty — the default — derives it from the base URL the browser reached this service at (<base>/federation/acs/<id>, which global.publicBaseUrl pins). Set it to the entityID the partner was configured with: it becomes the Issuer of the outbound AuthnRequest, the WS-Federation wtrealm, the SAML 1.1 providerId, this relationship's SP metadata entityID, and the audience an inbound assertion must name — which is a REFUSAL since 2026-09-12, so a partner that knows this service by another name needs this set. The assertion consumer URL stays derived, because it is an address a browser must be able to reach.

attributes.name: fedEnabled
attributes.what: TRUE/FALSE. A relationship is created DISABLED and nothing about it does anything until it is turned on: a half-configured partner that silently accepted assertions would be the failure this whole register exists to prevent.

attributes.name: description
attributes.what: One line per thing that has happened to this relationship.

attributes.name: fedSsoUrl
attributes.what: WHERE THE BROWSER IS SENT. The partner's SAML Single Sign-On service, its SAML 1.1 inter-site transfer service, its WS-Federation passive endpoint, or its OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint. Required in every protocol, because a relationship with nowhere to send anybody cannot begin.

attributes.name: fedTokenUrl
attributes.what: The partner's token endpoint, for the authorization code flow. THIS IS ONE OF THE TWO URLS THIS SERVICE WILL ACTUALLY DIAL — see federation_http.js, which is the only outbound request in this repository and argues why a configured URL is a different thing from a registered one.

attributes.name: fedUserinfoUrl
attributes.what: The partner's UserInfo endpoint, or any endpoint that answers JSON about the bearer of an access token. OPTIONAL for OIDC, where the ID Token usually carries enough, and the ONLY source of attributes for a plain OAuth 2.0 partner whose access token is opaque. The second URL this service will dial.

attributes.name: fedJwksUri
attributes.what: The partner's JWKS. FETCHED — which is the exact opposite of what oauthJwksUri on an application entry does, and the difference is the whole argument in federation_http.js: that one is a URL an unauthenticated caller REGISTERED, this one is a URL an administrator CONFIGURED. Leave it empty and paste the keys into fedJwks instead if this service is not to make the call.

attributes.name: fedEmailsUrl
attributes.what: A SECOND PROFILE ENDPOINT, for a provider that publishes a person's verified address apart from the rest (GitHub's /user/emails). Dialled with the same access token and under the same policy as fedUserinfoUrl, and only for a relationship whose provider profile reads it. Its failure costs the address, never the sign-in.

attributes.name: fedJwks
attributes.what: The partner's public keys as a JWKS document, verbatim. Read BEFORE fedJwksUri and never refreshed, so a relationship carrying this makes no outbound request for keys at all.

attributes.name: fedTrustAnchor
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY. The Entity Identifier of one of this realm's Trust Anchors (/admin/oidfed). Set, the OP named by fedPeer is resolved through its Trust Chain to that anchor, its endpoints and keys are the openid_provider metadata the chain vouches for, and this service registers with it AUTOMATICALLY under its own Entity Identifier, signing its requests and token-endpoint authentication with its ES256 key — so fedSsoUrl, fedTokenUrl, fedJwks, fedJwksUri, fedClientId and fedClientSecret are not read. Empty, the relationship is configured by hand as always.

attributes.name: fedSigningCertificate
attributes.what: THE PARTNER'S SIGNING CERTIFICATE, base64 DER — the same spelling a ds:X509Certificate carries and the same one samlSigningCertificate uses on an application entry, so one certificate has one spelling across this service. It is what every SAML and WS-Federation assertion is verified against, and it is the single attribute standing between this service and an endpoint anybody could assert anything at.

attributes.name: fedClientId
attributes.what: THIS SERVICE'S client_id AT THE PARTNER. Ours, issued by them — not to be confused with an oauthClientId on an application entry, which is a client's id here.

attributes.name: fedClientSecret
attributes.what: THIS SERVICE'S SECRET AT THE PARTNER, in the clear, in a directory where every bind succeeds. It is a REAL credential at a REAL foreign service, which is a stronger statement than anything else in this directory — see the header. Never written to the audit log and never printed on a page.

attributes.name: fedResponseMode
attributes.what: HOW THE AUTHORIZATION RESPONSE COMES BACK. Empty, the default: query for code, and form_post (OAuth 2.0 Form Post Response Mode) for an OpenID Connect response type carrying an ID Token or an access token. form_post, which Sign in with Apple requires whenever a name or an address is asked for, arrives as a cross-site POST, so a browser sends it no SameSite=Lax cookie. fragment, OpenID Connect only, is the default of those response types in the specification: the answer is in the URL fragment, and a page with one script here posts it on. It puts the ID Token in the browser's history, which form_post does not: use it only for a partner that cannot post. query cannot carry an ID Token or an access token.

attributes.name: fedAllowedTenants
attributes.what: MICROSOFT, ANY TENANT ONLY: the tenant ids whose people may sign in, one per value. fedPeer then holds {tenantid}, filled from each token's tid, and a token from a tenant not listed is refused. Empty refuses every tenant.

attributes.name: fedTeamId
attributes.what: APPLE ONLY: the Apple Developer team id, the iss of the client secret this service signs for every token request.

attributes.name: fedKeyId
attributes.what: APPLE ONLY: the id of the Sign in with Apple key, the kid of the client secret this service signs.

attributes.name: fedClientSigningKey
attributes.what: APPLE ONLY: THE PRIVATE KEY this service signs its client secret with (the .p8 file Apple issued, a P-256 key in PKCS #8 PEM). It is a credential at Apple. It is sealed under the key-encryption key wherever keys persist, never shown and never written to the audit log. A client secret signed with it lives five minutes and is minted per token request.

attributes.name: fedAuthorizeParams
attributes.what: EXTRA AUTHORIZATION REQUEST PARAMETERS, one per value, written `<name>=<value>`, for a provider that needs one (Twitch's `claims`, to be sent an address). OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 only. The parameters this service sets itself — response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, state, scope, nonce, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, response_mode, request and request_uri — are refused here, because one of them changed here would undo a check this service makes.

attributes.name: fedTokenAuth
attributes.what: HOW THIS SERVICE AUTHENTICATES AT THE PARTNER'S TOKEN ENDPOINT: client_secret_basic (the default, which RFC 6749 section 2.3.1 says a server MUST support) or client_secret_post, for a partner that reads the secret only from the body. With no fedClientSecret this service is a public client and neither applies. tls_client_auth (RFC 8705 section 2.1) authenticates with the relationship's TLS client certificate (fedClientCertificate) and sends no assertion and no secret; it is for fedFapi 1-advanced alone, and a relationship naming it without that profile is not ready.

attributes.name: fedScope
attributes.what: The scope asked of the partner. `openid profile email` is the default for an OIDC relationship and there is no default for an OAuth 2.0 one, because what an OAuth 2.0 authorization server will give you is entirely local to it.

attributes.name: fedResponseType
attributes.what: code (the default), id_token, or one of OpenID Connect's other four: id_token token (implicit), code id_token, code token and code id_token token (hybrid). `id_token` with form_post is the shape that needs NO back channel and therefore no token endpoint, no client secret and no outbound request — which is the only way to federate with an OIDC partner from a deployment that has no egress at all. An ID Token from the authorization endpoint must carry the nonce, and c_hash and at_hash wherever a code or an access token came with it.

attributes.name: fedIdTokenSignedResponseAlg
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY. THE ONE ALGORITHM the partner signs this relationship's ID Tokens and Logout Tokens with — what was registered at the partner as id_token_signed_response_alg (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 3.1.3.7 step 7, Back-Channel Logout 1.0 section 2.6). A token signed with any other is refused, even one the partner's key verifies. Empty, the default: any algorithm of the verifying key's family that federation.jwtAlgorithms allows. Set it: an empty one accepts a token signed by another of the partner's keys under another algorithm.

attributes.name: fedUserinfoSignedResponseAlg
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY. The algorithm a SIGNED UserInfo answer must be signed with — what was registered at the partner as userinfo_signed_response_alg (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 5.3.2). A signed answer is verified against the partner's keys whether or not this is set; set, one under another algorithm is not used. Empty, the default: a JSON answer, or a signed one under any algorithm of its key's family.

attributes.name: fedUserinfo
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY. TRUE, the default (and what an empty value means): the partner's UserInfo endpoint is asked with the access token at sign-in and at every refresh, and what it answers for the same sub is added to the ID Token's claims (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 5.3). FALSE: UserInfo is never asked, whatever fedUserinfoUrl or the discovery document names, and the person's claims are the ID Token's alone — for a partner whose UserInfo this relationship may not call, such as a FAPI 1.0 Advanced authorization server that serves its resource elsewhere.

attributes.name: fedRefreshTokens
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY. TRUE keeps the refresh token the partner issues at sign-in, sealed, with the session it started, and uses it to keep that session's identity current (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 12): every fedRefreshEverySeconds the session's tokens are refreshed, a new ID Token must name the same iss and sub, and UserInfo must still answer for that sub. A refresh the partner refuses, or an answer that fails those checks, ENDS the session. The token dies with the session. FALSE, the default: the partner's tokens are used once, at sign-in, and discarded — nothing here holds a credential at another service, and the partner's own sign-out and Shared Signals are what end the session early.

attributes.name: fedRefreshEverySeconds
attributes.what: With fedRefreshTokens on: how often, in seconds, a session's tokens are refreshed. Empty: when the access token expires (its expires_in), or hourly where the partner names no expiry. The scheduler job federation.partner-refresh looks every fifteen seconds.

attributes.name: fedRegister
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY, with fedDiscovery. TRUE has this service REGISTER ITSELF at the partner (OpenID Connect Dynamic Client Registration 1.0, RFC 7591) at the registration_endpoint its discovery document names, whenever the relationship holds no fedClientId or holds one registered with another issuer — at the start of a sign-in, or by an administrator's register-partner. The client_id and secret the partner issues are written to fedClientId and fedClientSecret (sealed). What is registered is this relationship: its assertion consumer service, response type, client authentication, the algorithms set here and, for request objects, the public key that signs them. FALSE, the default: the client is registered at the partner by hand.

attributes.name: fedRegisteredIssuer
attributes.what: The issuer fedClientId was registered with by fedRegister. Written by the registration; clear it, with fedClientId, to register again at the next sign-in.

attributes.name: fedRequestObject
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY. Send the authorization request as a Request Object (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 6, RFC 9101): request (by value) or request_uri (by reference — the partner fetches it, once, from /federation/request/{id}/{handle}). Signed under fedRequestObjectSigningAlg with this realm's key. Empty, the default: a plain authorization request.

attributes.name: fedRequestObjectSigningAlg
attributes.what: The algorithm a Request Object is signed with: RS256 (the default), PS256 or ES256 under this realm's key, or none — an UNSIGNED one, which Core 6.2 allows only by reference over https; a warning: the partner then has only the TLS of the fetch to say this service wrote it.

attributes.name: fedWebFinger
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY, with fedDiscovery. TRUE answers /federation/webfinger/{id}, where a PERSON types an identifier (acct:user@host or a URL) and this service asks that host who the person's OpenID Provider is (OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 section 2, RFC 7033). A WARNING: the host dialled is one a caller chose — this service's one argued exception of that kind among the federation requests, under the outbound policy (no internal address in product mode, no redirect, the cap). The issuer found must begin with fedPeer, which bounds it to the partner an administrator configured; the person is shown the issuer and continues only by pressing a button. FALSE, the default, refuses.

attributes.name: fedDiscovery
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY. TRUE reads the partner's endpoints and its jwks_uri from its discovery document, {fedPeer}/.well-known/openid-configuration, at the start of every sign-in (OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 section 4), whose issuer must be fedPeer exactly; fedSsoUrl, fedTokenUrl, fedUserinfoUrl and fedJwksUri are then not read. The address is derived from fedPeer, which an administrator configured, and never from a request. FALSE, the default: the endpoints are configured by hand.

attributes.name: fedFapi
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY. The FAPI client profile used when this service signs a person in at the partner (#931). Empty, the default, is today's OpenID Connect relying party. 1-advanced (FAPI 1.0 Advanced) forces response type code id_token, PKCE S256 and a PS256 request object by value, presents the relationship's TLS client certificate (fedClientCertificate) to the token and UserInfo endpoints so the partner can bind its access tokens to it (RFC 8705), authenticates with private_key_jwt or, where fedTokenAuth is tls_client_auth, with that certificate, and does not use DPoP. 2-security (FAPI 2.0 Security Profile) forces discovery, a pushed authorization request, response type code, PKCE S256, private_key_jwt and DPoP. 2-message-signing adds a PS256 request object inside that push and a signed authorization response (JARM). A 2.x profile forces private_key_jwt whatever fedTokenAuth says. This service does not act as a CIBA client, and only 1-advanced presents a client certificate.

attributes.name: fedInitiateLogin
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT ONLY. TRUE answers this relationship's login initiation endpoint, /federation/initiate-login/{id}, which the partner registers as initiate_login_uri (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 4): a sign-in the PARTNER starts, naming itself in iss, which must be fedPeer. A login_hint is passed on, and a target_link_uri is followed only to a path on this service. FALSE, the default, refuses it: a page anywhere could otherwise start a sign-in in a person's browser.

attributes.name: fedBinding
attributes.what: Which binding the outbound SAML AuthnRequest goes on: HTTP-Redirect (the default, and what every identity provider supports) or HTTP-POST. It says nothing about the response, which arrives on whatever binding the partner sends it on and is accepted on all of them.

attributes.name: fedSignRequest
attributes.what: Sign the outbound AuthnRequest with THIS service's key. OFF by default: most identity providers do not require it, and a partner that does will refuse the request in a way that names the problem. When it is on, the certificate to configure at the partner is the one on this service's own SAML metadata.

attributes.name: fedUsernameSource
attributes.what: WHICH INCOMING VALUE IS LOOKED UP AT LINK-AT-FIRST-SIGN-IN, and matched under any-existing — a claim name for OIDC/OAuth 2.0, a SAML Attribute Name for the others. Empty means the subject itself: the NameID, or `sub`. It does not name an entry this sign-in CREATES: that name is the relationship and the partner's stable subject (#358).

attributes.name: fedSubjectClaim
attributes.what: PLAIN OAUTH 2.0 ONLY: the member of the profile endpoint's answer that is the partner's stable identifier for the person, as a dotted path (id, data.id). Empty keeps what this service has always done — sub, then id, then user_id. It is the SUBJECT, the half of a federation link that must never change, which is not the username (fedUsernameSource). An OpenID Connect partner's subject is the ID Token's sub, which OpenID Connect Core section 5.7 makes the only stable one, and a consumer provider's is its profile's.

attributes.name: fedAttributeMap
attributes.what: ONE VALUE PER MAPPING, written `<incoming name>=<LDAP attribute>`. What is NOT listed here still arrives — federation_map.js has a default table covering the ordinary OIDC claims, the SAML urn:oid: names and the WS-Federation claim URIs — so this is for the partner's own inventions rather than for the names everybody uses.

attributes.name: fedAutocreateUsers
attributes.what: DYNAMIC PROVISIONING: create a directory entry the first time this partner signs somebody in. Written TRUE when a relationship is created in development and FALSE in product (mode.defaultsFederatedAutocreate()); a relationship that stores neither reads the same way. OFF means the person must ALREADY have an entry here — provisioned ahead of time, by SCIM or by hand — and a sign-in for somebody who does not is refused, because a session needs an entry to be the subject of. (Until 2026-09-14 OFF gave a session and no entry; a stable subject made that state impossible.)

attributes.name: fedUpdateUserAttributes
attributes.what: Update the person's directory attributes on EVERY sign-in from the latest assertion or token. ON by default, which is what this service always did. OFF writes the partner's attributes only when this sign-in CREATED the entry, so a pre-provisioned person — or one somebody has since edited — keeps what the directory says. Which relationship and issuer a person came through is recorded either way.

attributes.name: fedProvisionGroups
attributes.what: BUILD GROUP MEMBERSHIPS FROM THE PARTNER'S TOKEN (#358). OFF by default, and a missing value is off. On, each group name the assertion carries becomes a membership of the person this sign-in provisioned, on every successful sign-in. A group created this way is marked with this relationship. A name that already exists and is not marked as this relationship's is ignored, audited (STS-FED-0161) and the sign-in continues. A group that grants something by being held — a console group, a role's member group, an owner group, a group a policy names — is never created or joined (STS-FED-0164). It does not satisfy fedSubjectGroup: that rule runs before anybody is added.

attributes.name: fedProvisionCap
attributes.what: HOW MANY PEOPLE THIS RELATIONSHIP MAY CREATE. 0 is unlimited. Empty is unlimited for an enterprise partner; a CONSUMER or social provider's relationship is never unlimited by default: it is created with federation.consumerProvisionCap (10000 unless the realm says otherwise) written here, and an empty value means that setting. At the cap a new subject is refused STS-FED-0090; a person already linked still signs in. ldap.maxEntries remains the realm ceiling. Not a count of sign-ins — fedUsers is that.

attributes.name: fedProvisionIdleMinutes
attributes.what: DISABLE A PERSON THIS RELATIONSHIP IS THE ONLY SIGN-IN PATH FOR, once federationLastSeen is older than this many minutes. Empty or 0 is off: nobody is disabled for being idle. The entry and the link are kept. A person with a local userPassword, or a link through another relationship, is left alone. A partner's account-disabled signal is separate (STS-FED-0156) and blocks only that partner's sign-ins.

attributes.name: fedSubjectPolicy
attributes.what: HOW THE PARTNER'S SUBJECT BECOMES A LOCAL PERSON. The subject is the partner's own stable identifier — iss + sub, a persistent NameID and the partner's entity ID — and a person carries it as a federationLink. link-at-first-sign-in (the default; empty means it): a linked subject signs in; an unlinked one naming an existing person must first sign in HERE as that person — password, and a second factor where one is held or required — and only then is the link recorded and the partner's attributes written; one naming nobody gets a new entry namespaced to this relationship where provisioning is on. pre-linked: only a link signs anybody in. jit-namespaced: an unlinked subject always gets a NEW entry, <relationship>~<subject>, never an existing person. The subject is the partner's stable identifier, with a urn:uuid: folded to sub-<uuid>; it is not the mapped username. any-existing: the name the partner sent is matched straight onto a local person, as this service did before #109 — DEVELOPMENT ONLY, refused in product, and it lets this partner sign in any account it can name.

attributes.name: fedSubjectGroup
attributes.what: A RULE ON TOP OF THE POLICY: the person must be a member of one of these groups, each a cn or a DN. An entry this sign-in would CREATE is in no group, so with this set nobody is created. Empty: no group rule.

attributes.name: fedSubjectDomain
attributes.what: A RULE ON TOP OF THE POLICY: the mail domain the partner SENT (the mapped mail, or the mapped username where it is an address) must be one of these, and so must the local entry's mail where it has one. Compared case-insensitively and exactly: example.com does not admit sub.example.com. Empty: no domain rule.

attributes.name: fedHomeRealmDomain
attributes.what: HOME-REALM DISCOVERY (#148): an authorization request whose OpenID Connect Enterprise Extensions `domain_hint` is one of these goes straight to this partner's sign-in, unless the application names a partner of its own. Compared case-insensitively and exactly. A routing hint only — who is ADMITTED is fedSubjectDomain's.

attributes.name: fedSubjectPattern
attributes.what: A RULE ON TOP OF THE POLICY: a regular expression the local entry's DN must match WHOLE (it is anchored for you), such as uid=[^,]+,ou=users,.* — for an entry this sign-in would create, the DN it would be created at. At most 256 characters, no backreference and no quantifier applied to a group that is itself quantified, and it is tested against at most 1024 characters, so a pattern cannot be made to backtrack for minutes. Empty: no pattern.

attributes.name: fedMayAssertAdministrators
attributes.what: LET THIS PARTNER SIGN IN A CONSOLE ADMINISTRATOR. OFF by default, and off means a person in the Admin Read or Admin Write roster — or holding REMOTE_PEPS — is refused whatever else is true, a valid link included (STS-FED-0093). Turning it on makes this partner's signing key a key to the console for every administrator linked to it.

attributes.name: fedSignalEmailMatch
attributes.what: LET THIS PARTNER'S SHARED SIGNALS NAME A PERSON BY MAIL. OFF by default: a Security Event Token from a transmitter with this partner's issuer names a person by `iss_sub`, through the person's federationLink. On, an `email` subject matches the one person with that mail address as well — an address is not an identifier (OpenID Connect Core section 5.7), so only for a partner whose addresses this realm trusts.

attributes.name: fedSignalsEnabled
attributes.what: RECEIVE THIS PARTNER'S SHARED SIGNALS. OFF by default on a sign-in relationship, and the whole point of an `ssf` one, where it is written ON at creation. Off, no push is accepted for this relationship and the poll job skips it; fedEnabled must be on as well.

attributes.name: fedSignalsIssuer
attributes.what: THE PARTNER'S SSF ISSUER, when it is not fedPeer. Empty — the default — uses fedPeer, which is right for an OpenID Connect partner whose transmitter shares its issuer. A SAML 2.0 or WS-Federation partner's entityID is usually NOT its SSF issuer URL, so set it there. The configuration document is fetched from /.well-known/ssf-configuration under it (SSF 1.0 section 7) and must name it, and every SET's iss must be it.

attributes.name: fedSignalsDelivery
attributes.what: HOW THE PARTNER'S EVENTS ARRIVE: poll (RFC 8936, the ssf.foreign-poll job, the default) or push (RFC 8935, to /federation/signals/{id} with an authorization header only this realm and the partner know). Read when the stream is created; delete and create it again to change it.

attributes.name: fedSignalsEvents
attributes.what: THE EVENT TYPE URIS THE STREAM ASKS FOR (events_requested). None asks for whatever the partner supports.

attributes.name: fedSignalsTokenUrl
attributes.what: WHERE THIS REALM GETS AN ACCESS TOKEN FOR THE PARTNER'S STREAM MANAGEMENT, by client credentials. Empty uses fedTokenUrl — the same authorization server the sign-in relationship already dials.

attributes.name: fedSignalsClientId
attributes.what: THIS SERVICE'S client_id FOR THE PARTNER'S STREAM MANAGEMENT. Empty uses fedClientId.

attributes.name: fedSignalsClientSecret
attributes.what: THE SECRET FOR fedSignalsClientId, SEALED under the key-encryption key wherever keys persist and never shown. Empty uses fedClientSecret, sealed the same way.

attributes.name: fedSignalsScope
attributes.what: The scope asked for with client credentials. Empty asks for `ssf.read ssf.manage`, the CAEP Interoperability Profile's two (section 2.7.3).

attributes.name: fedSignalsBearer
attributes.what: A BEARER TOKEN THE PARTNER ISSUED, instead of client credentials. Sealed like fedSignalsClientSecret, and used whenever it is set.

attributes.name: fedSloUrl
attributes.what: THE PARTNER'S SAML 2.0 SingleLogoutService — where this service sends a signed <LogoutRequest> when a person signs out HERE (/logout), and where the <LogoutResponse> to the partner's own LogoutRequest goes. From the partner's metadata. Empty: the partner is never told of a sign-out here, and a LogoutRequest from it is still honoured but answered with nothing, because there is nowhere to send the answer. SAML 2.0 only: SAML 1.1 defines no logout at all.

attributes.name: fedSloBinding
attributes.what: Which binding a LogoutRequest or LogoutResponse this service sends the partner goes on: HTTP-Redirect (the default; the signature is over the query string) or HTTP-POST (an enveloped signature, on a real form with a real button — no script). A message FROM the partner is accepted on either.

attributes.name: fedEndSessionUrl
attributes.what: THE PARTNER'S OpenID Connect end_session_endpoint (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0), from its discovery document. When a person signs out HERE, the sign-out page offers to send them there with the partner's own ID Token as id_token_hint, this relationship's client_id, and this relationship's single logout endpoint as post_logout_redirect_uri — which the partner must have registered. The ID Token is kept on the session only while this is set. Empty: the partner is not told.

attributes.name: fedAcceptSignout
attributes.what: HONOUR THE PARTNER'S SIGN-OUT: a SAML LogoutRequest, an OpenID Connect Back-Channel or Front-Channel logout, a WS-Federation cleanup. ON by default — the partner is the authority on the person's sign-on, and when it ends a session or disables an account there, this is the only signal that reaches here. Off, every one of them is refused (STS-FED-0123) and the session here lives its whole lifetime.

attributes.name: fedRequireSignedLogout
attributes.what: REQUIRE THE PARTNER'S SAML LogoutRequest AND LogoutResponse TO BE SIGNED, as saml-profiles-2.0-os section 4.4.4.1 says they MUST be. ON by default and ALWAYS on in product mode, where turning it off is refused (STS-FED-0132). Off — development only — accepts an UNSIGNED logout message, which lets anybody who can name a person's partner session end it: a partner under test that cannot sign yet is the only reason to. A signature that IS present is verified either way.

attributes.name: fedEncryptionKeyType
attributes.what: THE KIND OF KEY A PARTNER ENCRYPTS TO: rsa-3072 (the default for SAML 2.0 and WS-Federation) or ec-p256 (the default for OpenID Connect) — or, for OpenID Connect only, a post-quantum one (#82): x-wing (HPKE-10-KE, ML-KEM-768 + X25519) or ml-kem-768 (ML-KEM-768), an AKP key published in the relationship's JWKS with no certificate, from Internet-Drafts few partners implement yet. Changing it issues a new key of that kind at once and keeps the old one for federation.encryptionKeyGraceS, as a rotation does.

attributes.name: fedKeyManagementAlgorithm
attributes.what: HOW THE PARTNER WRAPS OR AGREES THE CONTENT KEY, and the only one accepted. XML (SAML 2.0, WS-Federation): rsa-oaep — XML Encryption 1.1's RSA-OAEP with SHA-256 and MGF1-SHA-256 — for an RSA key, ecdh-es (ConcatKDF, kw-aes256) for an EC one. JOSE (an OpenID Connect ID Token): RSA-OAEP-256 or RSA-OAEP for an RSA key, ECDH-ES, ECDH-ES+A128KW or ECDH-ES+A256KW for an EC one. WARNING: RSA-OAEP is OAEP over SHA-1, offered for a partner that has nothing newer; RSA-OAEP-256 is the one to use. rsa-1_5 and RSA1_5 are refused in every mode (Bleichenbacher). Empty means the default for the key type.

attributes.name: fedContentEncryptionAlgorithm
attributes.what: THE CIPHER OVER THE ASSERTION OR THE ID TOKEN, and the only one accepted: aes256-gcm (the default) or aes128-gcm for XML, A256GCM (the default) or A128GCM for JOSE. AES-CBC — XML Encryption's aes*-cbc and JOSE's A*CBC-HS* — is refused in every mode: the XML form is the padding oracle of Jager and Somorovsky (2011), and a partner that can do GCM in one can in the other.

attributes.name: fedAllowUnencrypted
attributes.what: ACCEPT A PLAINTEXT ASSERTION IN PRODUCT MODE. OFF by default, and off means a SAML 2.0 or WS-Federation assertion, or an OpenID Connect id_token by form_post, that is NOT encrypted to this relationship's key is refused (STS-FED-0140). WARNING: turning it on lets the partner send the person's NameID, mail, groups and every other attribute IN CLEAR through their browser — its history, its extensions and every TLS-terminating proxy on the way. Turn it on only for a partner that cannot encrypt, and prefer asking it to. Development mode accepts plaintext whatever this says.

attributes.name: fedEncryptionKey
attributes.what: THE KEY TABLE: one JSON row per key this relationship decrypts with — its kid, its key type, `current` or `previous`, its certificate and chain under this realm's Intermediate, and the private key, SEALED under the key-encryption key wherever keys persist. A `previous` row is kept until its retiresAt and then removed by the scheduler job federation.encryption-key-retire. Written only by create, rotate and that job; WITHHELD from every LDAP search in product and from every page and /admin-api reply, which publish the public half. The key type is a column so a hybrid post-quantum key can be a row beside the classical one once one is registered.

attributes.name: fedClientCertificate
attributes.what: OPENID CONNECT, fedFapi 1-advanced ONLY (#931). THE TLS CLIENT CERTIFICATE this service presents when it dials the partner's token and UserInfo endpoints: one JSON row holding a clientAuth certificate from this realm's TLS Client Issuing CA (subject CN=federation <id> client, a urn:sts:federation: subjectAltName), its chain, its x5t#S256, its validity, and the private key, SEALED under the key-encryption key wherever keys persist. It authenticates the client where fedTokenAuth is tls_client_auth (RFC 8705 section 2.1) and is what the partner binds its access tokens to (cnf.x5t#S256, section 3). Issued when fedFapi becomes 1-advanced, at the first sign-in that has none, or by the scheduler job federation.client-certificate-renew, which also renews it federation.clientCertificateRenewDays before it expires, with the same subject. Written only by those; WITHHELD from every LDAP search in product and from every page and /admin-api reply, which publish the public half to register at the partner.

attributes.name: fedAllowUnsolicited
attributes.what: Accept a response this service did not ask for — SAML 2.0's unsolicited Response, and SAML 1.1's ONLY mode of operation. OFF by default for SAML 2.0 and forced ON for SAML 1.1, because that profile has no request to be in response to. Turning it on for SAML 2.0 removes the InResponseTo check, which is worth knowing rather than worth hiding.

attributes.name: fedApplication
attributes.what: THE POINTER, and the whole of what this side stores about the partner: the identifier of its entry in ou=applications. Its entityID, its assertion consumer service, its redirect URIs and its certificate live THERE, where every protocol module already reads them. Copying any of them here would be the two-stores failure this repository is arranged to avoid.

attributes.name: fedAuthnMechanism
attributes.what: HOW THIS SERVICE AUTHENTICATES THE PERSON when this partner asks it to: password, password-mfa, webauthn, spnego — a Kerberos ticket the browser already holds, with no screen at all — wallet — a credential this realm issued, presented from the person's wallet — or federation, which sends them on to another relationship and is what makes this service an identity BRIDGE between two protocols. EMPTY MEANS THIS RELATIONSHIP SAYS NOTHING, which is not the same as password: it falls through to appFederationRelationship on the application entry and then to the sign-in screen, which is exactly what every relationship did before this attribute existed.

attributes.name: fedAuthnRelationship
attributes.what: WHICH RELATIONSHIP THE PERSON IS SENT TO, when the mechanism is `federation`. It names a SERVICE-PROVIDER-side relationship in THIS realm — the register is per realm, so an id from another one names nothing here — and it is checked when it is USED rather than when it is written, because the relationship it names can be disabled or deleted afterwards by somebody who never looked at this entry. Ignored by every other mechanism, and required by this one: readinessOf() names it.

attributes.name: fedRelease
attributes.what: WHICH ATTRIBUTES ARE RELEASED TO THIS PARTNER, by claim or attribute name. It FILTERS what /admin/claims, /admin/saml-attributes and the groups claim would otherwise put in an artifact for this audience, and it can touch nothing else — not sub, not iss, not exp, not a NameID. NO VALUES HERE MEANS NO POLICY, not release nothing; see the header, where the difference is argued.

attributes.name: fedFirstSeen
attributes.what: GeneralizedTime: when this relationship was first USED, which is not when it was created.

attributes.name: fedLastSeen
attributes.what: GeneralizedTime, the most recent use.

attributes.name: fedAuthentications
attributes.what: How many credentials have crossed this relationship. ASSIGNED on every change — a counter that accumulated values would be nonsense — and it is a live number in a directory entry, which a real directory would not hold.

attributes.name: fedUsers
attributes.what: How many distinct identities have crossed it. Counted against fedLastUser, so it counts a CHANGE of user rather than a set: right for the ordinary case and an undercount for somebody alternating between two partners. Stated here because it is a number on a page.

attributes.name: fedLastUser
attributes.what: The most recent identity. On the entry rather than in memory because the entry is the store.

attributes.name: fedApplicationUse
attributes.what:
THE SAME TWO COUNTS, SPLIT BY THE APPLICATION THE SIGN-IN WAS FOR — one value per application, packed as `application|authentications|users|lastUser|lastSeen`. It exists because fedAuthentications answers "how much has crossed this relationship" and the map at /admin/federation/map has to answer "how much has crossed it FOR EACH of the applications configured to use it", which is a different question the moment a second application names the same partner.

IT IS SERVICE-PROVIDER SIDE ONLY, and that is not an omission. An identity-provider-side relationship names exactly ONE application (fedApplication), so its per-application count IS fedAuthentications and a second attribute holding the same number under another name is the copy that comes to disagree.

A VALUE IS WRITTEN ONLY FOR A PAIR THIS SERVICE IS CONFIGURED FOR, checked against the live configuration at the moment of the write rather than trusted from the request — see applicationConfiguredFor(). Without that check this attribute would be an unbounded list of strings anybody who can reach /federation/login/{id} chose, on the one entry in this directory whose contents decide whether an assertion is refused.

`|` IN EITHER FREE-TEXT FIELD IS REPLACED BY `~` ON THE WAY IN, which is the trade this format makes and it is stated rather than discovered: this is a packed counter drawn on a picture, not an identifier anything joins on. The application a row is FILED under is compared in the same packed spelling throughout, so a pair round-trips to itself whatever it is called.

attributes.name: fedLastError
attributes.what: WHY THE LAST ATTEMPT FAILED, in this service's own words. It is the most useful attribute here and it is why refusals are recorded rather than only logged: a federation that does not work fails at somebody else's service, and "the signature did not verify against the configured certificate" is the sentence that ends the argument about whose end is broken.

attributes.name: fedLastErrorAt
attributes.what: GeneralizedTime for the line above. Separate, so that an old error beside a recent success reads as history rather than as the current state.

group.note: No SCHEMA export. A group grants nothing by being a group.

objectClasses.name: top
objectClasses.what: The abstract class every entry carries.

objectClasses.name: groupOfNames
objectClasses.what: The class the container's own groups carry.

objectClasses.name: groupOfUniqueNames
objectClasses.what: Also treated as a group.

objectClasses.name: posixGroup
objectClasses.what: RFC 2307. Also treated as a group.

objectClasses.name: groupOfURLs
objectClasses.what: Also treated as a group. The page states no RFC number.

attributes.name: cn
attributes.what: The group's name, which names the entry (cn=<name>,ou=groups) and is what a roster or a role names the group by.

attributes.name: member
attributes.what: The group's members, one DN per value. Deleting a person leaves their DN here: the directory keeps no referential integrity.

attributes.name: description
attributes.what: What the group is for, as an administrator wrote it.

attributes.name: uniqueMember
attributes.what: The members of a groupOfUniqueNames group, one DN per value, read as member is.

attributes.name: memberUid
attributes.what: The members of a posixGroup (RFC 2307), one bare username per value, read beside member.

attributes.name: scimExternalId
attributes.what: SCIM's externalId of a Group, which /scim/v2 stores verbatim (models/scim/scim.tsp). The People section names it on people and groups.

attributes.name: stsPasskeyPolicy
attributes.what: The named passkey policy this group's members are held to, or `default`. Set on the group's page or with POST /admin-api/groups/set-policy, which accepts only a policy the realm holds.

attributes.name: stsLocalePolicy
attributes.what: The named locale policy this group's members are held to, or `default`. Set on the group's page or with POST /admin-api/groups/set-policy, which accepts only a policy the realm holds.

attributes.name: stsPasswordPolicy
attributes.what: The named password policy this group's members are held to, or `default`. Set on the group's page or with POST /admin-api/groups/set-policy, which accepts only a policy the realm holds.

attributes.name: stsAuthnPolicy
attributes.what: The named authentication policy this group's members are held to, or `default`. Set on the group's page or with POST /admin-api/groups/set-policy, which accepts only a policy the realm holds.

attributes.name: stsPostLoginPolicy
attributes.what: The named post-login policy this group's members are held to, or `default`. Set on the group's page or with POST /admin-api/groups/set-policy, which accepts only a policy the realm holds.

attributes.name: stsAttributePolicy
attributes.what: The named attribute policy this group's members are held to, or `default`. Set on the group's page or with POST /admin-api/groups/set-policy, which accepts only a policy the realm holds.

attributes.name: federationRelationship
attributes.what: On a group a federation relationship's group provisioning created: that relationship's id. A later sign-in through the relationship may add people only to groups carrying its mark.

attributes.name: mail
attributes.what: The address a notice to the group is sent to (#989). The operator's to set; nothing verifies it.

attributes.name: displayName
attributes.what: The name OpenID Provider Commands metadata shows for the group, where it differs from cn.

kerberosTrust.note: One entry per trust with another Kerberos realm.

objectClasses.name: top
objectClasses.what: The abstract class every entry carries.

objectClasses.name: stsKrb5Trust
objectClasses.what: This service's class for this register.

attributes.name: stsKrb5TrustData
attributes.what: The trust's whole record as one JSON value: the partner Kerberos realm, its NetBIOS name and domain SID, the type, the trust attributes and which keys are held. The attributes beside it mirror it for an ldapsearch. Written by the console and the management API.

attributes.name: stsKrb5TrustKeys
attributes.what: The trust's keys or shared passwords, as one JSON value sealed where keys persist. Withheld from every directory read.

attributes.name: trustPartner
attributes.what: The partner Kerberos realm, lower-cased, as Active Directory's trustedDomain object names it ([MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7). A mirror of the record, written with it.

attributes.name: flatName
attributes.what: The partner's NetBIOS domain name ([MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7). A mirror of the record, written with it.

attributes.name: securityIdentifier
attributes.what: The partner domain's SID, where the trust names one ([MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7). A mirror of the record, written with it.

attributes.name: trustDirection
attributes.what: 1 inbound, 2 outbound, 3 both ([MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7.12). Derived from which keys the trust holds: the incoming key accepts the partner's tickets, the outgoing key refers this realm's people to the partner.

attributes.name: trustAttributes
attributes.what: The trust's attribute bits as one integer ([MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7.9). A mirror of the record, written with it.

attributes.name: trustType
attributes.what: 2 where the partner is an Active Directory domain (the record names its SID), 3 for any other Kerberos realm ([MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7.15). Derived, written with the record.

oidfed.note: One entry per federation key, subordinate, anchor or mark.

attributes.name: stsOidfedKeys

attributes.name: stsOidfedEvent

attributes.what: The losing entryUUID of a two-process create race.

person.note: No SCHEMA export. One person is one entry, RDN uid.

objectClasses.what: RFC 2798 inetOrgPerson.

attributes.name: uid
attributes.what: The username, which names the entry (uid=<username>) and which every sign-in finds the person by, released as the preferred_username claim. Written when the entry is created; a rename is not an attribute edit.

attributes.name: cn
attributes.what: The person's common name, released as the name claim. On person's MUST list, so it cannot be emptied. An administrator, the person on /portal, SCIM or a federated sign-in writes it; in development an entry this service creates gets an invented one.

attributes.name: sn
attributes.what: The person's surname. On person's MUST list, so it cannot be emptied. Written as cn is, and released as the family_name claim.

attributes.name: givenName
attributes.what: The person's given name, released as the given_name claim. Written as cn is.

attributes.name: displayName
attributes.what: The name shown for the person, released as the nickname claim. Single-valued in RFC 2798.

attributes.name: mail
attributes.what: The person's email address, released as the email claim. Written by its own control (set-mail) rather than the attribute editor, because a change is verified and the former address is told.

attributes.name: userCertificate
attributes.what: Certificates stored on the person, as userCertificate;binary (base64 DER). A certificate from an outside certificate authority is an identity only as the one entry storing it, byte for byte. Written from the person's console page, /admin-api/users/add-certificate and remove-certificate, or an LDAP modify.

attributes.name: title
attributes.what: The person's job title, released as the job_title claim and mapped by SCIM.

attributes.name: employeeType
attributes.what: The person's relationship to the organisation, such as employee or contractor, released as the employee_type claim and mapped by SCIM.

attributes.name: telephoneNumber
attributes.what: The person's telephone numbers, released as the phone_number claim and mapped by SCIM.

attributes.name: mobile
attributes.what: The person's mobile numbers, released as the msisdn claim and mapped by SCIM.

attributes.name: street
attributes.what: The street part of the person's address, released in the address claim.

attributes.name: l
attributes.what: The locality (city) of the person's address, released in the address claim.

attributes.name: st
attributes.what: The state or province of the person's address, released in the address claim.

attributes.name: postalCode
attributes.what: The postal code of the person's address, released in the address claim.

attributes.name: c
attributes.what: The country of the person's address, released in the address claim: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, stored upper-case. Single-valued in RFC 4519.

attributes.name: postalAddress
attributes.what: The person's whole postal address as one formatted value, released in the address claim.

attributes.name: o
attributes.what: The organisation the person belongs to, released as the organization claim and mapped by SCIM.

attributes.name: ou
attributes.what: The organisational unit or division the person belongs to, released as the organizational_unit claim and mapped by SCIM.

attributes.name: departmentNumber
attributes.what: The person's department, released as the department claim and mapped by SCIM.

attributes.name: employeeNumber
attributes.what: The person's employee number, released as the employee_number claim and mapped by SCIM. Single-valued in RFC 2798.

attributes.name: preferredLanguage
attributes.what: The person's preferred language, in RFC 2798's Accept-Language syntax, released as the locale claim. Single-valued in RFC 2798.

attributes.name: labeledURI
attributes.what: A web page about the person: an http or https URL, optionally followed by a label. Released as the website claim.

attributes.name: manager
attributes.what: The DN of the person's manager. The shape of a DN is checked; the entry it names need not exist here.

attributes.name: schacDateOfBirth
attributes.what: The person's date of birth, stored YYYYMMDD (SCHAC's form), released as the birthdate claim. One value: the attribute editor refuses a second.

attributes.name: schacCountryOfCitizenship
attributes.what: The person's nationalities, one ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code per value, released as the nationalities claim. SCHAC's name.

attributes.name: schacPersonalTitle
attributes.what: The person's honorific, such as Dr, released as the Identity Assurance title claim. SCHAC's name.

attributes.name: salutation
attributes.what: A formal salutation for the person, released as the Identity Assurance salutation claim. This service's own name: no standard attribute type carries it.

attributes.name: birthFamilyName
attributes.what: The person's family name at birth, released as the Identity Assurance birth_family_name claim. This service's own name.

attributes.name: birthGivenName
attributes.what: The person's given name at birth, released as the Identity Assurance birth_given_name claim. This service's own name.

attributes.name: birthMiddleName
attributes.what: The person's middle name at birth, released as the Identity Assurance birth_middle_name claim. This service's own name.

attributes.name: alsoKnownAs
attributes.what: Other names the person is known by, released as the Identity Assurance also_known_as claim. This service's own name.

attributes.name: placeOfBirthCountry
attributes.what: The country the person was born in, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, released in the Identity Assurance place_of_birth claim. One value: the attribute editor refuses a second.

attributes.name: placeOfBirthRegion
attributes.what: The region the person was born in, released in the Identity Assurance place_of_birth claim. One value: the attribute editor refuses a second.

attributes.name: placeOfBirthLocality
attributes.what: The locality the person was born in, released in the Identity Assurance place_of_birth claim. One value: the attribute editor refuses a second.

attributes.name: schacGender
attributes.what: The person's gender as an ISO/IEC 5218 code, released as the gender claim (male, female, not known or not applicable). SCHAC's name, single-valued.

attributes.name: middleName
attributes.what: The person's middle name, released as the middle_name claim. This service's own name; one value.

attributes.name: timeZone
attributes.what: The person's time zone, an IANA zone name such as Europe/Stockholm, released as the zoneinfo claim. This service's own name; one value.

attributes.name: pictureUrl
attributes.what: The address of the person's picture, released as the picture claim. While the person has a profile photo this service holds, it is that photo's address. This service's own name; one value.

attributes.name: profileUrl
attributes.what: The address of the person's profile page, an http or https URL, released as the profile claim. This service's own name; one value.

attributes.name: scimExternalId
attributes.what: SCIM's externalId: the provisioning client's own identifier for the person, stored verbatim by /scim/v2 and read by nothing else.

attributes.name: userPrincipalName
attributes.what: The person's user principal name, read by certificate enrollment's smartcard-logon profile as the certificate's UPN. Nothing in this service writes it; a client supplies it.

attributes.name: stsWebauthnCredential
attributes.what: The person's registered WebAuthn public keys, one JSON value per passkey or security key. Public by design. Written by registration on /portal and the sign-in steps.

attributes.name: stsKrb5KeyInfo
attributes.what: The public half of the person's Kerberos keys, one JSON value: the key version number, the encryption types and when they were derived.

attributes.name: hobaPublicKey
attributes.what: The person's RFC 7486 HOBA client public keys, one value per key as `<kid> <base64 DER>`, registered at /.well-known/hoba/register. Public.

attributes.name: stsActivationExpires
attributes.what: When the pending activation link stops working.

attributes.name: stsPasswordResetExpires
attributes.what: When the pending password reset link stops working.

attributes.name: pwdChangedTime
attributes.what: When the person's password last changed (draft-behera-ldap-password-policy). Maintained by the password policy.

attributes.name: pwdHistory
attributes.what: Earlier password hashes, kept for the password policy's history rule (draft-behera-ldap-password-policy). Withheld from every read.

attributes.name: pwdReset
attributes.what: TRUE when the password must be changed at the next sign-in (draft-behera-ldap-password-policy).

attributes.name: pwdAccountLockedTime
attributes.what: Set while the account is disabled: 000001010000Z means an administrator, or SCIM's active: false, disabled it. Every door refuses the person while any value is present (draft-behera-ldap-password-policy).

attributes.name: stsBackupCodes
attributes.what: The person's recovery codes, one JSON value holding each code's hash and when it was used, and the counts. Issued when a second factor is first enrolled. Withheld from every read.

attributes.name: stsActivationToken
attributes.what: The scrypt hash of a pending activation link. Withheld from every read.

attributes.name: userPassword
attributes.what: The person's password as an scrypt hash, hashed on every write including an LDAP modify. Written by the sign-in, the portal, an administrator, SCIM or an LDAP modify, each through the password policy. Withheld from every read.

attributes.name: stsProfilePhoto
attributes.what: The person's profile photo record, one JSON value: which stored image is theirs, whose it was, and whether they declined a partner's copy. The image itself is not on the entry. Written only by the portal and a federated sign-in, and withheld from every read.

attributes.name: stsTotpCredential
attributes.what: The person's RFC 6238 authenticator secret, one JSON value. Sealed under the key-encryption key in product mode, and withheld from every read.

attributes.name: stsAppPassword
attributes.what: The person's app passwords, one JSON value holding each one's name, the doors it is scoped to, its scrypt hash and its last use. Withheld from every read.

attributes.name: stsPasswordResetToken
attributes.what: The scrypt hash of a pending password reset link an administrator or the person started. Withheld from every read.

attributes.name: stsKrb5Keys
attributes.what: The person's Kerberos long-term keys for every encryption type, derived from their password, as one sealed value. Password-equivalent, so withheld from every read, ciphertext included.

attributes.name: stsSelfIssuedSubject
attributes.what: The SIOPv2 self-issued subjects the person enrolled, one JSON value per subject: a DID or a JWK thumbprint URI, its label and who enrolled it. Whoever holds the key signs in as the person, so it is withheld from every read.

attributes.name: stsPublishedDid
attributes.what: Each did:web this realm publishes for the person, one JSON value per DID: its id, the DID, who holds its key, every version of its keys, its deactivation and, in realm custody, the sealed private key. Withheld from every read.

attributes.name: stsCibaUserCode
attributes.what: The scrypt hash of the CIBA user code the person set on /portal/ciba. Withheld from every read.

objectClasses.name: stsAttributePolicy
objectClasses.what: This service's class for an attribute policy: the attributes every person in a realm must hold. Named by the PROFILE (`cn=default`, or a named profile of the realm's own).

objectClasses.name: stsAttributeDefinition
objectClasses.what: This service's class for a custom attribute of a realm, in ou=attributeDefinitions, named by the attribute (`cn=<name>`).

attributes.name: stsAttributeRequired
attributes.what: The attributes every person in this realm must hold a value of, besides uid, cn and sn, which are always required. A list, or comma-separated. Any attribute a person may be given a value for: the inetOrgPerson schema, the credential catalogue, mail, and this realm's custom attributes. Enforced in product mode: a create without one is refused at every door, and an edit may not take one away. Default givenName, sn and mail.

attributes.name: description
attributes.what: What the profile or the custom attribute is for, for the next person.

attributes.name: stsAttributeLabel
attributes.what: A custom attribute's label, drawn beside its name.

attributes.name: stsAttributeSyntax
attributes.what: A custom attribute's syntax: string, integer, boolean, date, email, uri or dn. Its values are checked against it.

attributes.name: stsAttributeSingleValued
attributes.what: TRUE where a custom attribute holds one value, FALSE where it holds several.

attributes.name: stsAttributePortalVisible
attributes.what: TRUE where a person sees their own values of a custom attribute on the user portal's Overview. FALSE, or absent, by default.

attributes.name: stsAttributePortalEditable
attributes.what: TRUE where a person may change their own values of a custom attribute on the user portal. Implies stsAttributePortalVisible. FALSE, or absent, by default.

attributes.name: stsAttributePolicyPrecedence
attributes.what: Which named attribute policy applies where the person and their groups name several: the lowest, from 1 to 1000.

personAttributes.name: stsAttributePolicy
personAttributes.what: On a person or a group: the attribute policy it names, `default` or a named profile of the realm. One value.

objectClasses.name: stsAuthnPolicy
objectClasses.what: This service's class for an authentication policy: which mechanisms are accepted as a first and as a second factor, and when a second factor is required. The entry is named by the PROFILE (`cn=default`).

attributes.name: stsAuthnRequireSecondFactor
attributes.what: `if-held`: a person is asked for a second factor when they hold one (or their entry says stsMfaRequired). `always`: everybody in this realm is, and somebody who holds none is sent to enrol one at their next sign-in. This replaced authn.mfaRequired. There is no "never": a held factor is always asked for.

attributes.name: stsAuthnRequireSecondFactorForAdministrators
attributes.what: For anybody holding a console role (Admin Read or Admin Write) who holds no second factor. `offer`: they are shown the step that sets one up, with an Ignore button, at every sign-in. `always`: they must set one up before they are signed in — except the default realm's built-in administrator (admin.bootstrapUsername), who is only ever offered one, so a service is never left with nobody who can sign in. `if-held`: as everybody else, by the field above. WEAKER THAN `always`: an administrator on a password alone is an administrator anyone with the password is.

attributes.name: stsAuthnPasswordPrimary
attributes.what: A password on the sign-in screen. As a SECOND factor it is the password asked for after a wallet or other passwordless first factor.

attributes.name: stsAuthnPasswordSecondFactor
attributes.what: A password on the sign-in screen. As a SECOND factor it is the password asked for after a wallet or other passwordless first factor.

attributes.name: stsAuthnPasskeyPrimary
attributes.what: Any passkey (WebAuthn credential) the person holds, signing them in with no password. A passkey has no role: this row says, at each sign-in, whether any of them may be a first factor in this realm, unless the first factors of the authentication policy an application names (appAuthnPolicy) say otherwise.

attributes.name: stsAuthnSecurityKeySecondFactor
attributes.what: Any passkey (WebAuthn credential) the person holds, asked for after a first factor. A passkey has no role: this row says, at each sign-in, whether any of them may be a second factor in this realm, unless the second factors of the authentication policy an application names (appAuthnPolicy) say otherwise.

attributes.name: stsAuthnTotpSecondFactor
attributes.what: An RFC 6238 one-time code. Never a first factor: this service holds the same shared secret the app does. Off here, nobody may ENROL one; a person who already holds one is still asked for it, because an off switch that downgraded every enrolled account to a password alone would do something other than it says (this row replaced totp.enabled, and keeps its contract).

attributes.name: stsAuthnRecoveryCodeSecondFactor
attributes.what: A single-use code from a set the person generated. Off here, no new set may be generated; a set already held still works (this row replaced backupCodes.enabled, and keeps its contract).

attributes.name: stsAuthnEmailCodePrimary
attributes.what: A six-digit code mailed to the person's VERIFIED address. NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.1: "Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication", because a mailbox may be reached with a password alone, and mail may be read in transit or rerouted. Off by default for that reason; turn it on only where that is an accepted risk.

attributes.name: stsAuthnEmailCodeSecondFactor
attributes.what: A six-digit code mailed to the person's VERIFIED address. NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.1: "Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication", because a mailbox may be reached with a password alone, and mail may be read in transit or rerouted. Off by default for that reason; turn it on only where that is an accepted risk.

attributes.name: stsAuthnEmailLinkPrimary
attributes.what: A single-use link mailed to the person's VERIFIED address, which completes the sign-in only in the browser that started it. NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.1: "Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication", because a mailbox may be reached with a password alone, and mail may be read in transit or rerouted. Off by default for that reason; turn it on only where that is an accepted risk.

attributes.name: stsAuthnEmailLinkSecondFactor
attributes.what: A single-use link mailed to the person's VERIFIED address, which completes the sign-in only in the browser that started it. NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.1: "Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication", because a mailbox may be reached with a password alone, and mail may be read in transit or rerouted. Off by default for that reason; turn it on only where that is an accepted risk.

attributes.name: stsAuthnCertificatePrimary
attributes.what: A verified TLS client certificate: GET /tls/sign-in, or Continue with your certificate on the sign-in screen.

attributes.name: stsAuthnKerberosPrimary
attributes.what: GET /authn/spnego with a Kerberos ticket.

attributes.name: stsAuthnWalletPrimary
attributes.what: /authn/wallet with a credential this realm issued, or a SIOPv2 self-issued ID Token from an enrolled key. As a SECOND factor, the wallet presented after a password.

attributes.name: stsAuthnWalletSecondFactor
attributes.what: /authn/wallet with a credential this realm issued, or a SIOPv2 self-issued ID Token from an enrolled key. As a SECOND factor, the wallet presented after a password.

attributes.name: stsAuthnFederationPrimary
attributes.what: A sign-in asserted by a configured federation partner.

attributes.name: stsAuthnEmailCodeTtlS
attributes.what: From the moment it is sent. At most ten minutes, NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.2's bound for an out-of-band secret.

attributes.name: stsAuthnEmailCodeAttempts
attributes.what: How many wrong codes one sign-in step accepts before it is ended and the person starts again. The per-person and per-network rate limits apply as well.

attributes.name: stsAuthnEmailResendS
attributes.what: A new code or link replaces the last one, which stops working. At most three are sent for one sign-in step.

attributes.name: stsAuthnEmailFailureLimit
attributes.what: NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.2.2 asks for no more than 100. The person, and their administrators, are told, and the person turns it on again from the portal.

attributes.name: stsAuthnRememberedBrowserSkipsSecondFactor
attributes.what: OFF BY DEFAULT. On, a person signing in on a browser they chose to remember is not asked for their second factor again within the period below of last giving it on that browser. NEVER at the admin console, the user portal or the protocol debugger; never for an administrator; never while the sign-in's risk is medium or higher; and the sign-in is then ONE factor to every relying party — amr ["pwd"] and acr "1", as a password alone — so an application asking for "mfa" is refused it. The browser is recognised by a bearer cookie: whoever copies the cookie skips the second factor too, until the copy is caught.

attributes.name: stsAuthnRememberedBrowserDays
attributes.what: Counted from the last time the person gave their second factor on that browser. After it they are asked again, and giving it starts the period again.

attributes.name: description
attributes.what: What the profile is for, for the next person.

attributes.name: stsAuthnPolicyMechanism
attributes.what: On a NAMED authentication policy (#1148, #1237): a first-factor mechanism a sign-in it applies to allows — where the application (appAuthnPolicy) or one of the person's groups (stsAuthnPolicy) names it and its precedence is the lowest named — password, password-mfa, webauthn, spnego, wallet or federation, one value each. None allows every one the realm allows.

attributes.name: stsAuthnPolicySecondFactor
attributes.what: On a NAMED authentication policy (#1148, #1237): a second factor a sign-in it applies to allows — where the application (appAuthnPolicy) or one of the person's groups (stsAuthnPolicy) names it and its precedence is the lowest named — password, securityKey, totp, recoveryCode, emailCode, emailLink or wallet, one value each. None leaves the realm's authentication policy as it is.

attributes.name: stsAuthnPolicyPrecedence
attributes.what: On a NAMED authentication policy (#1237): which one applies where several are named for one sign-in — by the application (appAuthnPolicy) and by the person's groups (stsAuthnPolicy) — the lowest, from 1 to 1000, ties by name. 100 when absent.

personAttributes.name: stsMailFactor
personAttributes.what: Which emailed second factor this person opted in to: `code` or `link`. Absent: none. Set on /portal/mfa, cleared on /admin/mfa and after too many consecutive failures.

personAttributes.name: stsMailFactorFailures
personAttributes.what: Consecutive failed emailed codes or links, reset by a success. Maintained by this service.

objectClasses.name: stsLocalePolicy
objectClasses.what: This service's class for a locale policy: the language a realm's pages fall back to and gives a new person. Named by the PROFILE (`cn=default`, or a named profile an application or a group names).

attributes.name: stsLocaleDefault
attributes.what: A BCP 47 language tag (RFC 5646), such as en, fr-CA or zh-TW. Pages are drawn in it when the request, the person's preferredLanguage, the language chooser and the browser name nothing a catalog answers; dates and numbers are formatted for it even where no catalog does. Mail to a person whose entry names no language is written in it. Replaces the setting mail.defaultLanguage.

attributes.name: stsLocalePopulatePreferredLanguage
attributes.what: ON BY DEFAULT.
